test_dag.note: The first invocation without TMPDIR produced five environment errors because no default writable temporary directory was available. The read-only rerun used ephemeral /dev/shm and passed all 19 tests.

benchmark_tests.command: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 TMPDIR=/dev/shm python -m unittest discover -q -s artifacts/NC-020 -p test_benchmark.py

integer_polynomial.implementation: Independent sparse coefficient maps over Z[x,y,z], without benchmark.normalize_int or benchmark.eval_int
integer_polynomial.proof_basis: Equality of finite coefficient maps proves equality of the represented polynomials for every exact integer assignment; unequal maps were additionally checked using the recorded integer witnesses.

bitvector.implementation: Independent typed output-bit interpreter; did not call benchmark.brute_bv, benchmark.eval_bv, canonical_isa.eval_ast, or benchmark.make_case

controls.interpretation: The generator and full committed test suite validate generated labels, types, hashes, witnesses, and split separation. The standalone benchmark.audit function is only a report summarizer and silently summarizes adversarially mutated input without revalidation.

split_audit.near_duplicate_review: No exact pair-shape fingerprint crosses train, validation, or test. Fingerprints intentionally erase variable identities and constant values and group positive/negative variants inside a split; therefore they are a structural-disjointness check, not a semantic-distance theorem.
split_audit.historical_independence: NOT_ESTABLISHED. The audit confirms disjointness only for this newly generated benchmark and cannot establish independence from historical model training or pretraining data.

proof_scope.integer: Exact polynomial equality over unbounded mathematical integers for the committed +, -, and * ASTs only.
proof_scope.bitvector: Exact finite enumeration of output bits for every X,Y assignment at each declared width 3, 4, or 5. R and T are unreferenced.
proof_scope.floating_point: Two concrete ordinary Python binary64 counterexamples only; no universal floating-point theorem.
proof_scope.invalid_types: Strict rejection of the two mixed-type controls; they are not semantic non-equivalence examples within a common type.

limitations: The standalone benchmark.audit function does not validate arbitrary supplied cases; consumers must regenerate with produce and run the committed tests or add explicit validation before trusting a report.
Structural fingerprints are deliberately coarse and do not prove semantic novelty between algebraically related families.
No historical model-training or pretraining independence can be verified from these artifacts.
The repository contained unrelated dirty NC-000 evidence files, but audited NC-020 sources, dataset, dependencies, champion paths, and checkpoint paths matched the audited commit.
recommendations: Harden benchmark.audit to reject invalid record hashes, case IDs, labels, witnesses, typed ASTs, and cross-split family/fingerprint leakage instead of only summarizing input.
Keep the existing proof-scope language and historical-data caveat in downstream use.
Record this verifier identity and immutable commit in the owner-generated receipt before the task owner appends DAG PASS.
